items.abstract: <jats:p xml:lang="en">The swift emergence of agentic artificial intelligence (agentic AI) signifies not merely a new trend in automation but a fundamental transformation in the design, governance and execution of work. Unlike preceding waves of machine learning and generative AI (GenAI), which predominantly offered recommendations or generated content, agentic AI introduces software agents capable of perceiving context, making decisions, executing tasks across various systems and learning over time. Procurement serves as an exemplary domain for demonstrating this paradigm shift. It operates at the confluence of finance, supply chain, legal, risk, environmental, social and governance (ESG) and business stakeholders, managing complex, rules-intensive, high-value decisions. This paper posits that agentic AI will profoundly overhaul the procurement operating model, transitioning it from function-centric workflows to an AI-native hub that orchestrates autonomous agents, human experts and interconnected data. It outlines the practical aspects of agentic AI, explains why procurement is central to its adoption, and describes how capabilities such as autonomous sourcing, negotiation, onboarding and compliance monitoring reshape processes, roles and decision-making rights. Furthermore, it proposes an operating model blueprint for AI-native procurement, encompassing governance, risk management and policy systems. It examines the skills, behaviours and organisational structures necessary for effective human–AI collaboration. Ultimately, it offers a pragmatic roadmap for chief information officers (CIOs) and chief procurement officers (CPOs) and considers implications for other enterprise functions. This framework enables the design of procurement organisations that leverage the value of agentic AI while maintaining control, resilience and trust.</jats:p>
title: Agentic AI and the operating model shift : Redesigning enterprise procurement for the AI-native era

items.abstract: Autonomous AI agents capable of executing cloud 2 infrastructure operations introduce a new class of risk that 3 existing safety mechanisms address incompletely. LLM output 4 filters govern what the model says but not what the agent does; 5 static admission controllers enforce rules at deployment time 6 but not at agent runtime; human oversight mechanisms are 7 decoupled from real-time execution pipelines. This paper presents 8 a five-layer guardrail architecture intercepting at the tool-call 9 execution boundary, combining: (1) AWS Bedrock Guardrails 10 for LLM output interception; (2) Open Policy Agent (OPA) 11 evaluation against live infrastructure state; (3) confidence-delta 12 scoring via A/B model comparison; (4) human-in-the-loop (HITL) 13 approval gating with DynamoDB time-to-live auto-rejection; 14 and (5) CloudWatch audit telemetry with S3 rollback. Em15 pirical evaluation on live AWS (us-east-1) across 100 prompts 16 spanning five risk categories including 20 adversarial jailbreak 17 variants demonstrates 96% overall accuracy, 1% false positive 18 rate, 0% false negative rate on destructive operations, and 19 a 22× latency reduction for intercepted actions (347 ms vs. 20 8,099 ms). An iterative calibration study across four tuning cycles 21 documents convergence from 60% to 96% accuracy, providing 22 empirical evidence that multi-layer defense-in-depth is necessary 23 rather than merely sufficient for production-grade DevOps agent 24 governance. Total evaluation cost: $0.0017 USD. Implementation: 25 https://github.com/ManvithaP-hub/agentic-devops-guardrails
title: A Layered Guardrail Architecture for Agentic AI in Cloud-Native DevOps Pipelines: Design, Implementation, and Empirical Evaluation on Live AWS Infrastructure

<jats:p>Modern financial systems deliver essential services in highly regulated, zero-failure environments. Yet
unprecedented external pressures—geopolitical conflicts, economic instabilities, climate change, and the COVID-19
pandemic—have challenged the ability of financial regulators and institutions to maintain confidentiality, integrity,
availability, and consistency of these systems. Financial services increasingly leverage automation enabled by Artificial
Intelligence (AI) to enhance efficiency, manage demand, and mitigate risks, but in many deployments, the traditional
risk-based approaches are no longer viable. Therefore, regulators and institutions are exploring the implications of
automated operations.
The rationale is that AI-enabled automation and decision-making can be performed at greater velocity and scale than
pure human workflows. However, the risk-management posture requires stringent governance. Financial institutions must
clearly define and maintain human oversight in critical or harmful decision-making. For other responsibilities, the policy
permitting automated decision-making needs to be captured, expressed, and securely stored in sources that can be read
and interpreted by Generative AI for creating Operations Manuals and other organizational context documents, in order
to enable LLMs to explain operations and processes, as well as to ensure that AI agents are trained in accordance with
these policies.</jats:p>
title: Integrating Agentic AI and Generative AI into Cloud-Native DevOps Pipelines for Financial Payment Systems

items.abstract: <jats:p>This disclosure presents three batteries of adversarial testing conducted under the VATA framework, examining safety failure modes in cross-company three-node AI pipelines (Planner → Executor → Validator). Battery B32 establishes that pipeline safety is determined by Executor model identity, not individual model safety ratings-with DeepSeek as the sole consistent Executor vulnerability across all tested configurations. Battery B33 demonstrates that shared context poisoning amplifies pipeline penetration rate by 5x (4.4% to 22.2%), with the DeepSeek→GPT→Gemini configuration reaching 77.8%</jats:p>
title: Agentic Pipeline Integrity: Position-Dependent Safety Failure and Context Poisoning in Cross-Company Multi-Model AI Pipelines
Conclusion—Toward a New Paradigm in AI-Enhanced Learning and Work
